description_top: The happy path of a payment is three boxes and a database. This question is about the other paths: a bank call that times out and leaves you not knowing whether the customer paid, three retries at once, and a statement that disagrees with your books. A compact reference solution at the Staff bar (L6/L7): theory, a three-version design, technology choices against their rivals, an alternate path for a small business, and six challenges that break it. {DURATION} minutes, {SLIDES} numbered slides, with an interviewer, a candidate and a coach.

The thesis: exactly-once does not exist across a network boundary. So the design is at-least-once delivery, one effect per intent, a state for not knowing yet, and a reconciliation that finds what the rest missed, on an append-only double-entry journal.

IN THIS VIDEO
• Estimates from one scale line: 9 billion payments a month, 40,000 journal entries a second, 580 TB in seven years
• Why the partition key is the merchant and not the account, and what changes with a million one-time accounts
• Why Go, against Java virtual threads, Spring WebFlux, Python and Rust
• Gateway or direct processor: what a gateway buys, what it costs, the break-even
• Debezium against a polling relay and the other ways to read the log
• Six challenges: the timeout, three retries, a crash before the event, the hot merchant, 999,998 against 1,000,000, and how you would know first

HOW TO USE IT
Run the round cold first. Then watch once straight through. On the second pass, pause after each interviewer question and answer it first.

This is a scripted walkthrough, not a recording of a real interview, and the interviewer, candidate and coach are not real people. The voices are synthetic (Kokoro-82M, generated locally). Script, diagrams and the written design were produced with Claude Code. Numbers are back-of-the-envelope estimates for the exercise, labelled as given, illustrative or initial targets, not any company's real figures, and this is not any company's actual design. Not legal, accounting or compliance advice. The technical content has not been reviewed by a person.

post: "Retry with backoff" is the answer that double-charges a customer. The grade is on what you do instead.

I've published a {DURATION}-minute reference solution for a payment system and its double-entry ledger at the Staff bar: theory, a three-version design, and six challenges, on {SLIDES} numbered slides.
The idea that unlocks it: exactly-once does not exist across the bank boundary, so build one effect per intent, a state for "not knowing yet", and books you can reconcile.

What it goes into:
→ The bank timed out: an UNKNOWN state and an inquiry by your own reference
→ Why partition by merchant, not by account (and a million one-time cards)
→ Gateway or direct processor, with the break-even
→ Debezium, and what to use instead below 1,000 events a second
Best on a second pass: pause after each question and answer it first.
It's a scripted walkthrough with synthetic voices, built with Claude Code from design-room, my open-source system design interview simulator.
